models.name: RT-DETR r18 object detection
models.title: RT-DETR r18
models.subtitle: object detection
models.summary: Real-time transformer detector trained on COCO: 80 object classes with boxes and scores.

pipeline.call: model(out)[0]        # (N, 6): class_id, score, x, y, w, h

paper.title: DETRs Beat YOLOs on Real-time Object Detection

snippets.label: PyTorch
snippets.code:
from kornia.contrib.object_detection import RTDETRDetectorBuilder

detector = RTDETRDetectorBuilder.build("rtdetr_r18vd", image_size=480)
detections = detector(x)[0]        # (N, 6): class_id, score, x, y, w, h; x in [0, 1]

snippets.label: ONNX from the hub
snippets.code:
from kornia.onnx import ONNXSequential

# the same graph this page runs, downloaded from huggingface.co/kornia/ONNX_models
model = ONNXSequential("hf://models/kornia.models.detection.rtdetr_r18vd_480x480")
out = model(x.numpy())[0]          # (1, 300, 6): class_id, score, x, y, w, h

models.note: Resizes to 480x480 inside the graph, so any input size works; boxes come back in those coordinates.

models.name: Depth Anything V2 small
models.title: Depth Anything V2 small
models.subtitle: depth estimation
models.summary: Monocular relative depth from a single image, ViT-S encoder, 8-bit quantised.

pipeline.note: the ImageNet normalisation is part of the exported pipeline graph; in PyTorch apply kornia.enhance.normalize first

snippets.label: ONNX Runtime
snippets.code:
import onnxruntime as ort
import torch
import kornia as K

# model_quantized.onnx from huggingface.co/onnx-community/depth-anything-v2-small
sess = ort.InferenceSession("model_quantized.onnx")
x = K.geometry.resize(x, (364, 364))                       # a multiple of 14
x = K.enhance.normalize(x, torch.tensor([0.485, 0.456, 0.406]), torch.tensor([0.229, 0.224, 0.225]))
depth = sess.run(None, {"pixel_values": x.numpy()})[0]    # (1, 364, 364) relative inverse depth

models.note: Input side must be a multiple of 14; the page uses 364. Output is relative inverse depth, shown with a colour map.

models.name: YuNet face detection
models.title: YuNet
models.subtitle: face detection
models.summary: Tiny face detector with five facial keypoints, a few milliseconds per image.

paper.title: YuNet: A Tiny Millisecond-level Face Detector

snippets.label: PyTorch
snippets.code:
import kornia as K
from kornia.contrib import FaceDetector, FaceDetectorResult

detector = FaceDetector()                 # YuNet, pretrained
faces = detector(x * 255.0)[0]            # (N, 15): box, 5 keypoints, score; x in [0, 1]
for face in [FaceDetectorResult(f) for f in faces]:
    print(face.top_left, face.bottom_right, face.score)

models.note: Backbone exported from kornia with dynamic height and width; box decoding and NMS run in JavaScript on the page.

models.name: XFeat keypoints and matching
models.title: XFeat
models.subtitle: keypoints + matching
models.summary: Accelerated features: keypoints with 64-d descriptors, matched against a warped copy of the same frame.

paper.title: XFeat: Accelerated Features for Lightweight Image Matching (CVPR 2024)

snippets.label: PyTorch
snippets.code:
from kornia.feature import XFeat

xfeat = XFeat.from_pretrained(top_k=512)
feats = xfeat.detectAndCompute(x)[0]                  # keypoints (N, 2), scores (N,), descriptors (N, 64)
idx0, idx1 = xfeat.match(feats["descriptors"], feats_other["descriptors"], min_cossim=0.82)

models.note: The network runs on the frame and on an affine-warped copy; NMS, scoring, descriptor sampling and mutual-nearest-neighbour matching run in JavaScript, checked against kornia at build time.

models.name: KeyNet + HardNet
models.title: KeyNet + HardNet
models.subtitle: detector + descriptor
models.summary: The classic two-stage pipeline: a learned keypoint detector, then a 128-d patch descriptor, matched against a warped copy.

paper.title: Key.Net: Keypoint Detection by Handcrafted and Learned CNN Filters (ICCV 2019); HardNet: Working hard to know your neighbor's margins (NeurIPS 2017)

snippets.label: PyTorch
snippets.code:
import kornia.feature as KF

detector = KF.KeyNetDetector(pretrained=True, num_features=300)
descriptor = KF.LAFDescriptor(KF.HardNet(pretrained=True))
lafs, responses = detector(gray)                        # local affine frames on a (B, 1, H, W) image
descs = descriptor(gray, lafs)                          # (B, 300, 128)
match_dists, idxs = KF.match_mnn(descs[0], descs_other[0])

models.note: Single-scale on the page: NMS on the response map, a 48-px window around each keypoint resized to a 32x32 patch, then the descriptor. kornia's KeyNetDetector adds a scale pyramid and affine frames.

models.name: TinyViT-5M classification
models.title: TinyViT-5M
models.subtitle: ImageNet classification
models.summary: A 5-million-parameter vision transformer distilled on ImageNet-22k, fine-tuned on ImageNet-1k: top-5 classes for a frame.

pipeline.call: model(out).softmax(-1)   # (B, 1000); normalisation is inside the exported graph, apply kornia.enhance.normalize in PyTorch

paper.title: TinyViT: Fast Pretraining Distillation for Small Vision Transformers (ECCV 2022)

snippets.label: PyTorch
snippets.code:
import torch
from kornia.models.tiny_vit import TinyViT
from kornia.enhance import normalize

model = TinyViT.from_config("5m", pretrained=True).eval()     # ImageNet-1k head
x = normalize(x224, torch.tensor([0.485, 0.456, 0.406]), torch.tensor([0.229, 0.224, 0.225]))
probs = model(x).softmax(-1)                             # (B, 1000)

models.note: 224x224 input, ImageNet normalisation; the page shows the five most likely ImageNet classes.
